arrival_rate.consequence_for_the_budget: a budget frozen from an early measurement is overrun later. The budget must be sized against the HIGH end of the arrival rate, and the cost is a higher skip rate early rather than an overflow late.
arrival_rate.finding: NO. Mean game length falls monotonically as the move policy trains -- 287.9 plies at iteration 3 to 166.9 at iteration 20, a 42% fall in 17 iterations -- and the arrival rate rises inversely with it, from 292 to 492 completed setup episodes per iteration (+68%). The queue drained to 214 by iteration 6 and then grew monotonically from iteration 16: 386, 476, 566, 718, 890.
not_established: where the mean game length settles: 20 iterations is 3% of a 640-iteration run
any strength claim; a shorter game is not a better game

outcome_mix.reading: 0.25% draws under the real current-policy tandem signal, against 83% under Agent 3's uniform-random legal fixture. This is the confound decision D9-B set out to remove, and it is removed: almost every tandem game is decisive, so the setup learner's outcome term carries signal rather than noise.

arrival_rate.question: does the completed-setup-episode arrival rate stay stationary while the tandem system trains? The setup budget is fixed before h0, so a rising arrival rate is the one thing that can overflow Agent 3's queue, which raises rather than evicting.

At the iteration-20 rate the frozen budget of 572 sits below arrivals at the production budget. P8 (now at 50% of capacity, with four windows of headroom) and the pre-window overflow check turn that into a clean early stop rather than a dead process, but it is still an early stop. carry_forward_for_agent_6.detail: beta saturates at its UPPER bound 1.0 for 97.5% of setup iterations -- the mirror of the lower-bound pinning D5 was raised to fix, and far past Agent 3's own pinned_fraction_limit of 0.5. The safety function is intact (max KL 0.0141 against the 0.08 hard limit, P3 never tripped) but the regulation function is gone: beta has no upward headroom. This also QUALIFIES the concentration reading -- a beta 59x Agent 3's final 0.0171 restrains the setup policy, and this rehearsal cannot separate that restraint from the outcome-signal effect. Agent 4 may not tune the KL (D9-B section 6), so the constants are unchanged.

readiness_reason.setup_alpha_indexing_unresolved: SetupTrainingConfig.alpha is indexed by the SETUP iteration. In tandem that counter runs slower than the move counter whenever the budget exceeds the arrival rate, so the anneal does not complete: at 125 setup updates alpha ends 2.24x above the paper endpoint 0.004091. Common contract section 8 defines the exponent against 'N, frozen by Agent 4', which is the twelve-hour ITERATION count. Decision D9-B section 6 forbids Agent 4 tuning alpha, so this is surfaced, not decided. Agent 4's reading -- offered, not applied -- is that indexing alpha by the move iteration resolves it, because the anneal then completes over the twelve hours regardless of how many setup updates the arrival rate permits.

Both are measured against this frozen N below. The common contract wins over the paper (section 2) and Agent 4 may not amend it without the operator, so the contract form is what is frozen here.
